Interface InventoryManager

All Known Implementing Classes:
InventoryManagerImpl
public interface InventoryManager
Central manager for player inventory GUI sessions with stack-based navigation.

The InventoryManager maintains a per-player stack of InventoryViews, enabling hierarchical menu navigation (push/pop pattern). It also manages a registry of InventoryProviders that define how inventories are created and rendered.

Navigation Model

Each player has an independent view stack. Opening a new menu pushes it onto the stack; going "back" pops the current view and reopens the previous one.

  • push(Player, String, InventoryContext) — Opens a new view on top of the stack
  • pop(Player) — Removes the current view and returns to the previous
  • invalid reference 
    #replace
    — Swaps the current view without growing the stack
  • clear(Player) — Clears the entire stack and closes the inventory

Provider Registry

Providers are registered with unique string IDs and are used to create views on demand. Providers can be registered programmatically or loaded from configuration.

Usage Example

InventoryManager manager = KLibrary.getInstance().getServiceProvider()
        .getInventoryManager().orElseThrow();

// Register a custom provider
manager.registerProvider(myCustomProvider);

// Open a menu for a player
InventoryContext context = InventoryContext.builder()
        .player(player)
        .plugin(plugin)
        .build();
manager.push(player, "main_menu", context);

// Navigate back
manager.pop(player);

  • Method Details

    • push

      void push(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull String providerId, @NotNull @NotNull InventoryContext context)
      Pushes a new inventory view onto the player's navigation stack and opens it.

      The view is created by the registered InventoryProvider matching the given provider ID. If no provider is found, this method does nothing.

      Parameters:
      player - the player to open the inventory for; must not be null
      providerId - the ID of the registered inventory provider; must not be null
      context - the context for this inventory session; must not be null

    • pop

      void pop(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Pops the current inventory view from the player's stack and opens the previous one.

      If the stack becomes empty after popping, the player's inventory is closed. If the stack is already empty, this method does nothing.

      Parameters:
      player - the player whose current view should be popped; must not be null

    • openReplace

      void openReplace(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull String providerId, @NotNull @NotNull InventoryContext context)
      Replaces the current inventory view with a new one.

      This method replaces the current GUI visually but still pushes it into the stack.

      Parameters:
      player - the player whose current view should be replaced; must not be null
      providerId - the ID of the registered inventory provider; must not be null
      context - the context for the new inventory session; must not be null

    • update

      void update(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player, @NotNull @NotNull InventoryContext context)
      Updates the current inventory view with a new context without changing the stack depth. This is useful for pagination.
      Parameters:
      player - the player whose current view should be updated; must not be null
      context - the new context for this inventory session; must not be null

    • clear

      void clear(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Clears the player's entire inventory stack and closes any open inventory.

      All tracked views for the player are removed from the active view registry.

      Parameters:
      player - the player whose stack should be cleared; must not be null

    • registerProvider

      void registerProvider(@NotNull @NotNull InventoryProvider provider)
      Registers an inventory provider, making it available for use with push(Player, String, InventoryContext) and
      invalid reference 
      #replace
      .

      If a provider with the same ID is already registered, it will be replaced.

      Parameters:
      provider - the provider to register; must not be null

    • unregisterProvider

      void unregisterProvider(@NotNull @NotNull String providerId)
      Unregisters an inventory provider by its ID.

      Any currently open views created by this provider will continue to function but no new views can be created from it.

      Parameters:
      providerId - the ID of the provider to unregister; must not be null

    • getProvider

      @NotNull @NotNull Optional<InventoryProvider> getProvider(@NotNull @NotNull String providerId)
      Retrieves a registered provider by its unique ID.
      Parameters:
      providerId - the provider ID to look up; must not be null
      Returns:
      an Optional containing the provider if found, or empty if not registered

    • clearProviders

      void clearProviders()
      Removes all registered providers from the registry.

      This is typically called during plugin reload to prepare for re-registration.

    • shutdown

      void shutdown()
      Shuts down the manager, cancelling the global update task, closing all active inventories, and clearing all internal state.

      This should be called during plugin disable to ensure clean shutdown.

    • getActiveViewId

      @NotNull @NotNull Optional<String> getActiveViewId(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Gets the ID of the currently active (topmost) view for the player.
      Parameters:
      player - the player to query; must not be null
      Returns:
      an Optional containing the active view's provider ID, or empty if the player has no open managed inventory

    • getStackSize

      int getStackSize(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Gets the depth of the inventory navigation stack for the player.

      A value of 0 means no managed inventory is open. A value of 1 means one view is open (no back history). Values greater than 1 indicate the player has navigated through multiple menus.

      Parameters:
      player - the player to query; must not be null
      Returns:
      the number of views in the player's stack (0 if none)

    • hasPrevious

      boolean hasPrevious(@NotNull @NotNull org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Checks if the player has a previous view in their navigation stack.
      Parameters:
      player - the player to query; must not be null
      Returns:
      true if there is a previous view (stack size > 1)
